title: Letters to His Son
author: Philip Stanhope, Lord Chesterfield
blurb: A worldly English lord's private letters to his son on charm, manners, attention and getting on in society — the 18th century's guide to being liked.

resent.e: She resented being left out of the plan.

attention.e: Give the recipe your full attention.

learning.e: Her learning showed in every answer.

cards.title: Hide your watch
cards.text: Don't show off your knowledge. Keep it like a watch in your pocket: bring it out when someone asks the time, not every minute to show you own one.
cards.quote: Wear your learning, like your watch, in a private pocket
cards.qMean: Don't show off what you know.
cards.qLife: Answering a question simply instead of lecturing about it.

cards.title: Don't seem wiser
cards.text: Never try to look smarter or more educated than the people you're with. It makes them resent you.
cards.quote: Never seem wiser, nor more learned, than the people you are with.
cards.qMean: Don't act cleverer than the people around you.
cards.qLife: Not correcting a friend's grammar at dinner.
cards.cap: William Hogarth, The Holland House Group · public domain

cards.title: Do it well or not at all
cards.text: Whatever is worth doing is worth doing well, and nothing is done well without attention — even dancing and dressing.
cards.quote: ver is worth doing at all, is worth doing well
cards.qMean: If something is worth doing, do it properly.
cards.qLife: Writing a thank-you note carefully, not in five seconds.
cards.cap: The York Minuet, 18th-century print · public domain

cards.title: Seize every moment
cards.text: Know what time is worth; use every moment. No laziness, no putting off till tomorrow what you can do today.
cards.quote: Know the true value of time; snatch, seize, and enjoy every moment of it.
cards.qMean: Value your time and use it fully.
cards.qLife: Finishing a small task now instead of adding it to tomorrow's list.
cards.cap: Lord and lady with Death and the hourglass, after Dürer · public domain

cards.title: The art of pleasing
cards.text: Being liked is a skill — necessary and hard. It can't be fully reduced to rules; watch people and learn.
cards.quote: The art of pleasing is a very necessary one to possess; but a very difficult one to acquire.
cards.qMean: Being pleasant to others is important but hard to learn.
cards.qLife: Noticing what makes a colleague smile and doing more of it.
cards.cap: Wanstead Assembly at Wanstead House by Hogarth · public domain

cards.title: Fools lie most
cards.text: In his experience the biggest fools are the biggest liars; he judges people's honesty by their intelligence.
cards.quote: the greatest fools are the greatest liars.
cards.qMean: The most foolish people tend to lie the most.
cards.qLife: The friend with wild excuses is rarely the sharpest.
cards.cap: William Hogarth - A Rake's Progress - Tavern Scene · public domain
